column1: # LOG-TEXT-DIVERGENCES.tsv - declared exceptions to G-LOGFILE's MESSAGE CONTENT check.
# The count checks in LOG-PORTMAP.tsv cannot see a message that is PRESENT but WRONG.
# One funnel emitted only the `err=` half of "error handling VT action action={} err={}"
# and every count was green; the same stage then dropped the space before a placeholder
# four times in its own fix commit (`mode:Flags { ... }` for `mode: <value>`). So the gate
# also compares each live emission's text against the reference call preserved as a
# comment above it, with PLACEHOLDER CONTENTS normalised and nothing else - spacing is the
# kind               one of: identity-rename, error-name-literal, abbreviated-comment,
# port_file          the Rust file the divergence lives in.
# reference_message  the normalised message from the preserved reference comment.
# port_message       the normalised message the port emits. EMPTY for stale-comment,
#                    which is about a comment with no emission of its own.
# reason             mandatory. A declaration with no reason is RED.
# Rows key on the MESSAGE PAIR, never on a line number: LEDGER.tsv's rustty-side anchors
# have already drifted up to 70 lines on rows closed earlier in this plan because
# restoration moves code, and a declaration keyed on a line would rot the same way.
# A declaration that matches NOTHING is RED - a waiver that outlives what it excused is
# how an exception becomes permanent. Delete it in the commit that fixed the text.
# `stale-comment` rows are N20: preserved comments quoting reference calls that do not
# exist at the pin, stranded by our own Phase 6 pin advance. Nothing emits them, so
# nothing is wrong today; the risk is a future stage reading the comment and faithfully
# restoring a call the reference never had.
# The cap is a RATCHET, both ways, like every other number in this gate.
